title: Hitcher: Efficient GPU-based Vector Search via Cluster-Centric Kernel and Hitch-Ride Ordering

problem.claim: GPU-based vector search systems have limited query throughput and latency.

gap.claim: Existing query-centric kernels fail to reuse shared-memory data across queries, while batch-based reordering prolongs latency because each query waits for its slowest task.

contributions.claim: Hitcher uses a cluster-centric GPU kernel to batch computation on the same data for multiple queries and improve GPU utilization.
Hitcher uses hitch-ride ordering to preserve query arrival order while batching computation across queries to reduce query latency.
Hitcher can offload computation tasks to the CPU and utilize multiple GPUs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report up to 22× lower P99 query latency than state-of-the-art GPU-based vector query processing systems.
The authors report up to 9× higher query throughput than state-of-the-art GPU-based vector query processing systems.

narrative_sequence.summary: Similarity-based vector search supports applications including search, recommendation, and LLMs.
GPU-based vector search systems are limited in query throughput and latency.
Query-centric kernels waste opportunities to reuse shared-memory data, and batch-based reordering prolongs latency through slowest-task waiting.
Hitcher combines a cluster-centric GPU kernel, hitch-ride ordering, CPU offloading, and multi-GPU utilization.
The authors report substantially lower P99 latency and higher throughput than state-of-the-art GPU-based vector query processing systems.

source_observation.claim: Batching computation across queries that access the same data can enable data reuse and improve GPU utilization.

interpretation.claim: Work organization around shared data may be more efficient than independently organizing computation around each query.

application.claim: For workloads with repeated data access across concurrent queries, consider data-centric batching in the accelerator kernel.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach benefits workloads without substantial cross-query data reuse.

unknowns: Datasets, workload configurations, and hardware details are not specified.
Baseline identities and experimental methodology are not specified.
The abstract does not quantify the effects of CPU offloading or multi-GPU utilization separately.
